trials.rationale: Measured facts: the independently measured original baseline step_ms is 108.594/108.516 ms per rank (max-rank median 108.594). The separately collected nsys step window on the rank whose NCCL kernels are short (the later-arriving rank; cross-rank clock alignment is unverified, so early/late identity is not asserted) spans 136.7 ms and contains 3986 compute kernels whose union busy time is only 42.2 ms (~31% device occupancy), plus 13 DDP bucket allreduce kernels totaling 35.0 ms, of which only 13.3 ms overlap compute (21.7 ms exposed), followed by ~1.7 ms of optimizer add_ kernels; there is a single 15.9 ms compute-free gap at 119.0-134.9 ms while the last small buckets and the 10.5 ms, 158 MB wte/wpe bucket (call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b; 12 further bucket reduces under call d0938de87369efd500322679, 2 invocations of the c10d::allreduce_ family covering 13 observed bucket collectives over 497,759,232 FP32 gradient bytes) drain after backward. nccl_tuning shows RING/SIMPLE decisions and ~29 GB/s effective bus bandwidth, i.e. the collectives are PCIe-bandwidth-bound at frozen gradient volume, and the DDP reducer configuration (bucket_cap_mb=25, gradient_as_bucket_view=True, default allreduce hook) is created by the frozen adapter, so bucket layout or comm-hook edits are not an available boundary. The dominant, addressable cost is therefore host-side dispatch of ~4000 tiny eager kernels (micro_batch=1 x seq 128 x 4 accumulated microbatches) plus the exposed comm tail, which no per-operator or per-module rewrite can recover. The one coherent editable boundary covering both is the complete project invocation: replace run() with a lazily-built CUDA Graph executor that warms up eagerly, captures the source's verbatim step (in-buffer gradient zeroing, 4 no_sync-accumulated forward/backward microbatches with exactly one gradient allreduce pass completing on the last backward, SGD foreach=False update, torch.cuda.synchronize() completion boundary) inside the actual adapter invocation, and replays it every subsequent invocation. Replay re-executes the identical recorded kernels on the same static buffers (inputs are fixed tensors; reset() restores weights in-place into the same storages), so numerics stay bitwise-equal to eager execution and the exact cross-rank gradient equality, global-batch reference checks, FP32 policies, workload identity and completion boundary are preserved. Per the binding contract, CUDA Graph replay does not rerun Python hooks, so the whole project bundle (group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, target project.invoke) is explicitly replaced via execution_plan scope; lazy capture during the harness warmup invocations (warmup=2) is legitimate setup, no measurement boundaries or thresholds change, and lifecycle allocator metrics keep their frozen definitions.

trials.rationale: Scope: the single project invocation group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (project.invoke, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0, phase run) is the coherent editable boundary because the installed accepted bundle trial-11e4128fb3-param-1fde4884 already replaces this whole call with a CUDA-graph executor, and the repair it needs (capture-time mask construction) can only be made inside that whole-invocation replacement; warmup, capture, averaging, replay and fallback are one unit. Measured facts: the accepted current revision measured step_ms 104.006 (ranks 104.046/103.967) vs parent 108.920/109.872, inside the <=114.024 limit, but the candidate's own declared routes in the accepted AB/BA receipts and in the quality/coverage diagnostic are 'fallback:eager-parent:setup-failure-capture:RuntimeError' on both ranks: the graph path never executed in any measured or profiled run, so the ~5 ms gain is warmup-attributed, not the intended mechanism. The concrete failure is deterministic: RuntimeError 'Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture unless the CPU tensor is pinned' raised at transformers-5.16.1 masking_utils.py:603 eager_mask (torch.where(mask, torch.tensor(0.0, device=mask.device, dtype=dtype), min_dtype)) reached from modeling_gpt2.py:583 create_causal_mask inside the graph1 capture forward (inputs/observations/previous-after/candidate_diagnostics-4123e6d6.json). Current discovery on this revision corroborates the eager structure that replay is meant to remove: 3999 compute kernels per step with non-NCCL device busy of only ~28.9-29.2 ms per rank (nsys rank-1 union 64.06 ms minus 34.89 ms NCCL), and 13 RING_LL bucket allreduces = the two c10d::allreduce_ calls (d0938de87369efd500322679 x12 at 7,087,872 elements, b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b x1 at 39,385,344 elements) covering all 124,439,808 FP32 gradient elements; the non-waiting rank's NCCL busy (12 x ~2.0 ms + ~10.4 ms = 34.89 ms) already matches the clean synthetic collective_calibration medians (1.966-1.985 ms and 10.549-10.612 ms) at exactly these sizes, so the collectives run at their achievable rate for this SHM/PCIe transport and hold no rate headroom at frozen volume; rank-0's 255.06 ms NCCL kernel sum is in-kernel waiting (diagnostic), not wire time. The optimizer step is ~1.7 ms (aten::add_.Tensor groups in optimizer_step phase). Therefore the serialized device-work floor is roughly 29 + 34.4 + 1.7 = ~65.5 ms plus launch/skew, while today's clean eager step is 104.0 ms: ~35-40 ms of host-side dispatch gaps remain the dominant recoverable cost, recoverable only at this whole-invocation boundary, not by per-operator or per-module edits, and comm-rate or bucket-layout edits have no measured headroom (calibration; DDP reducer configuration is created by the frozen adapter). affected_calls lists all 1526 observed calls descending from the invocation in current discovery; the two discovery profiler markers (profiler._record_function_enter_new/exit for 'opop::0') are framework annotations outside the project work and are excluded. Rank maxima are never summed with the hook-perturbed profiled wall (1222/1215 ms), which is used only qualitatively.

exceptions.message:
During CUDA graph capture, autograd node 'torch::autograd::AccumulateGrad' has a stale reference to the default stream (stream 0) from warmup. This will invalidate the capture because cudaStreamWaitEvent on the default stream pulls a non-capturing stream into the graph.

To fix, either:
  (a) Run warmup on the same stream that capture will use, or
  (b) Delete references to the loss / autograd graph (e.g. `del loss`) before capture, or
  (c) Call torch.autograd.graph.set_override_stale_capture_stream(True) to automatically redirect stale nodes to the capturing stream.

trials.rationale: Scope: the whole project invocation (group 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb, project.invoke call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0, phase run, 1 invocation on ranks 0/1) under execution_plan, replacing the installed bundle trial-11e4128fb3-param-1fde4884 which already writes this call. This is the only coherent editable boundary: warmup, graph capture, bucket-flat averaging, replay, validation and eager fallback are one unit inside the executor, and the repair the previous round needs (capture-time stream discipline) can only be made there. Concrete failure being repaired (inputs/previous-feedback.txt + observations/previous-after/candidate_diagnostics-4123e6d6.json, deterministic on both ranks): trial-f1097548f9's capture-safe mask fix WORKED - the earlier 'Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors' mask-scalar error is gone from the diagnostics - but graph1 capture now dies one step later, at _build line 274 (torch.autograd.grad inside the capture), with RuntimeError "During CUDA graph capture, autograd node 'torch::autograd::AccumulateGrad' has a stale reference to the default stream (stream 0) from warmup". Cause: the build's eager parent warmups run loss.backward() on the default stream, so the persistent parameters' AccumulateGrad nodes record stream 0, which always invalidates capture. Consequence: the only route observed was 'fallback:eager-parent:setup-failure-capture:RuntimeError', the graph path never executed, and the single screening measurement ran the eager step behind the executor at step_ms 120.372511 (ranks 120.372511/120.315863), exceeding the 114.02413995 limit (1.05 x original baseline 108.594419) - rejected as no_valid_parameter_candidate (n_complete=0, n_fail=1). So both the intended mechanism and the constraint hinge on this one capture blocker. Why this scope and not others (current discovery on revision d3b4c6ba): the accepted version measures ~104.0 ms median max-rank vs parent ~108.9 and limit 114.024, with every timed invocation executing the source's eager step; nsys shows 3999 compute kernels per step with non-NCCL device busy of only ~29 ms per rank, and 13 RING bucket allreduces - the two c10d::allreduce_ calls d0938de87369efd500322679 (x12, 7,087,872 elements) and b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b (x1, 39,385,344 elements) covering all 124,439,808 FP32 gradient elements - whose non-waiting-rank NCCL busy (34.89 ms) already matches the clean collective_calibration medians (1.985 ms and 10.612 ms) at exactly these sizes, so the collectives are PCIe-bound at the frozen 497,759,232 bytes and hold no rate headroom; rank-0's 255.06 ms NCCL kernel sum is in-kernel waiting (diagnostic), not wire time, and is never summed with rank maxima or with the hook-perturbed profiled wall (1222/1215 ms). The optimizer add_ kernels cost ~1.7 ms. The serialized device floor is therefore roughly 29 + 34.4 + 1.7 = ~65.5 ms plus launch/skew, while the eager step measures ~104 ms: ~35-40 ms of host-side dispatch of ~4000 tiny kernels is the dominant recoverable cost, removable only by whole-invocation replay, not by per-operator or per-module edits; comm-rate or bucket-layout edits have no measured headroom and DDP configuration belongs to the frozen adapter. Worker API verified on the measured environment (worker-environment.json, torch 2.13.0+cu129): torch.autograd.graph.set_override_stale_capture_stream exists and its documented default behavior raises exactly the observed error for stale default-stream references while enabled=True redirects stale non-capturing streams to the capture stream; torch.cuda.graphs.make_graphed_callables itself warms up on a side stream with torch.autograd.grad, the documented capture protocol. affected_calls is the invoke call plus all 1525 observed descendants in current discovery (the complete step, including the two c10d::allreduce_ calls, which the executor's eager bucket-flat averaging keeps issuing inside the measured step); the two opop::0 profiler markers are framework annotations outside the project work and are excluded.

intent.goal: Minimize maximum-rank clean step_ms for the source's complete accumulated training step, taking aligned rank maxima before the median over repeats. Retain the original step_ms <= 1.05x original-baseline constraint, all workload, precision, full quality and exact rank-replica requirements and the completion boundary. Communication kernel duration remains a separately profiled diagnostic, not wire time or the primary score.

invariants: Workload identity (request.workload; gpt2_ddp_training.py:148): each measured invocation is exactly one complete accumulated training step with world_size=2, micro_batch=1, sequence_length=128, accumulation_steps=4 on the declared GPT-2 config (n_layer=12, n_embd=768, n_head=12, vocab_size=50257, n_positions=1024): effective batch 8, 1024 tokens per step.

FP32 precision everywhere with TF32 disabled: model built with .float() (gpt2_ddp_training.py:27), torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32=False, torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False, torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest') (common.py:34-42; request notes 'Precision and state policies').

Deterministic fixtures: initial weights from torch.manual_seed(20261020) (gpt2_ddp_training.py:25) and per-rank synthetic token inputs from seed 31000+rank with labels=input_ids (gpt2_ddp_training.py:30-33); required so independent workers reproduce the same reference; assets is empty by design.

Loss/gradient semantics: each microbatch's cross-entropy loss is divided by accumulation_steps and accumulated (gpt2_ddp_training.py:42), so the accumulated gradient must match rank-0's serial single-GPU reference over the exact same global batch of 8 sequences within grad_atol=1e-06 / grad_rtol=1e-04 (gpt2_ddp_training.py:67-77; request quality).

Exact cross-rank gradient equality: after the last microbatch backward every parameter.grad must be bitwise identical across the 2 ranks, checked with torch.testing.assert_close(atol=0.0, rtol=0.0) against rank 0's broadcast replica (gpt2_ddp_training.py:80-86; request notes 'Discrete exact comparison'); reproduced in observe().

Optimizer update rule: SGD(lr=0.001, momentum=0.0, weight_decay=0.0) (gpt2_ddp_training.py:60); post-update parameters must match the reference within parameter_atol=1e-06 / parameter_rtol=1e-04 (gpt2_ddp_training.py:88-91; request quality).

Required communication happens inside the measured step: the gradient allreduce must complete on the last backward (request.communication='required'), and the accumulated loss must be finite (gpt2_ddp_training.py:65).

Completion boundary and timed-work division: the step ends with torch.cuda.synchronize() on every rank after optimizer.step(), and optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) plus the whole accumulation belong to the timed invocation (gpt2_ddp_training.py:36-45,102-105; request notes 'One measured invocation').
Every measured repeat starts from the identical initial weights restored outside timing (gpt2_ddp_training.py:99-100,107-114), so per-invocation observations remain comparable across repeats.
Numerics-affecting model settings: dropout fully disabled (resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.0) and use_cache=False (gpt2_ddp_training.py:26; request notes 'Precision and state policies').
The validator negative control must reject a +1 corrupted gradient at the workload tolerances (common.py:79-84; request notes quality semantics (d)); reproduced in observe().

Scoring semantics are fixed (request notes): per-rank step time, maximum across aligned ranks, then median over repeats, with step_ms constrained to <= 1.05x the original baseline; the adapter changes none of these aggregation or threshold values.
